title: Amen Thompson, Rockets Lock in Five-Year, $208 Million Extension
dek: Rockets guard Amen Thompson and the Houston franchise have agreed to a five-year, $208 million contract extension that includes a 10% trade kicker before Thompson's final rookie-scale season, per ESPN's Shams Charania. Thompson, the fourth overall pick in 2023, averaged 18.3 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 5.3 assists last season and finished eighth in Defensive Player of the Year voting.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Thompson's deal is worth $208 million over five years with a 10% trade kicker, locking the young two-way guard into the Rockets' core after a first-round playoff loss to the Lakers.
bottom_line: The deal is locked with the union agreement and requires no further approval. What remains to clarify is the year-by-year salary structure, whether the extension begins immediately or after the 2026-27 season, and the extent of any performance escalators or no-trade protections that could affect Houston's roster flexibility heading into the 2026-27 season.
body: Amen Thompson and the Houston Rockets have agreed to a five-year, $208 million contract extension that includes a 10% trade kicker, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. Thompson, the fourth overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, was entering the final year of his four-year rookie-scale contract. He will earn $12.3 million this season under the new deal.

Thompson averaged 18.3 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 5.3 assists for the Rockets last season and recorded 1.5 steals per game. He finished eighth in voting for Defensive Player of the Year. In the playoffs, Thompson elevated his production to 19.2 points, 7.0 rebounds, 5.7 assists, 2.0 steals, and 1.2 blocks per game while playing 44 minutes a night. However, Houston fell short to the Los Angeles Lakers in the first round.

Thompson came from Overtime Elite and has developed into a cornerstone piece for the Rockets' rebuild. The extension represents a long-term commitment to the young guard as the franchise attempts to build around his two-way potential.
